_doc: News access gating (#178, parent #150). What the player is ALLOWED to read on the industry wire, as opposed to what the market engine publishes — the engine always publishes everything (so the seed stream, and therefore replay, is identical whether or not anything is unlocked); this file decides which lanes reach the player's eyes. Three access lanes, each a different currency: PUBLIC (free — lot talk, the trade magazine, factory recall/incentive bulletins: vague, late, or already public), PAID (a data subscription — the block's actual numbers, a rival's actual percentages: the same events you already hear about, quantified), and STAFFED (a used car manager on the desk — forward calls, per manager-roles-channel-desk.md §3 'advise = free on hire'). A lane's `requires` names an unlock id; `null` is free. Lane matching is by SPECIFICITY, not array order: an exact source+reliability rule beats a source wildcard, which beats a reliability wildcard (ties fall back to declaration order), so a new voice can be slotted in anywhere in the list. All costs are first-pass placeholders tuned in the S14 balance pass (#286).

_lanesDoc: source '*' / reliability '*' are wildcards. The first lane is the free catch-all, so a voice added to the news catalog without a lane of its own FAILS OPEN — readable rather than silently unreadable. Same philosophy as #177's source fallback: a copy or config gap must never swallow news about something that really happened. A test cross-checks every (source, reliability) pair the catalog can publish against these lanes, so an unintended free lane is caught at review, not in play.
